biography: Paul Allen, a name synonymous with speed and a touch of audacious flair, hails from the quaint countryside of Oxfordshire, England. His journey into the world of motorsport began, rather unexpectedly, with a beat-up go-kart gifted by his grandfather on his tenth birthday. What started as a leisurely hobby quickly morphed into an all-consuming passion. Allen's raw talent was undeniable, tearing up local karting circuits with an aggressive, yet controlled, driving style. He progressed through the ranks, securing victories in Formula Ford and Formula Renault before catching the eye of Caterham Superlight. His debut season was a whirlwind, punctuated by podium finishes and the occasional spectacular crash – a testament to his 'win-or-bust' mentality. Now, at 30, Allen stands at the peak of his career, a seasoned racer known for his daring overtakes and unwavering self-belief. While a championship title remains elusive, his electrifying performances continue to captivate fans and intimidate rivals alike.
drivingStyle: Allen's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos.' He's known for his late braking and aggressive corner entries, often flirting with the limits of adhesion. Tire management isn't his strongest suit; he tends to push the rubber to its absolute maximum, sacrificing longevity for short bursts of blistering pace. Under pressure, Allen either thrives or implodes spectacularly; there's rarely an in-between. He relishes wheel-to-wheel combat and isn't afraid to make a daring move, even if it means risking it all.

careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2020 Le Mans 24 Hours, costing his team a likely victory and leaving him heartbroken.
